terra.problem: Saying the whole job is about serving the people leaves out Josiah's instruction to serve the LORD as well as His people (verse 3).
The passage does not say the people were not handed a bill or that Josiah covered everything himself. His officials also contributed.
The cookie-jar comparison does not make sense as a sound and does not match the action of giving willingly.
The text says the officials gave willingly, not that they gave gladly or that none of them sighed or gave side-eye.
The passage names contributors but does not say whether their giving was secret at the time.
Hilkiah, Zechariah and Jehiel are named without identifying them as chief officials of the house of God, and Conaniah is named without identifying him as an officer of the Levites.
The passage assigns the tasks but does not say nobody traded them.
The passage describes the assigned jobs, but does not say everybody knew whose task was whose.
The passage says the Passover animals were roasted according to the regulation. It does not say the other offerings were boiled according to a regulation.
The passage does not establish how long drying would take or that roasting was much quicker.
The passage does not say the crowd was hungry or give that as a reason the offerings were brought quickly.
The closing line is a generic platitude rather than Papa Dorin's natural, distinctive voice.
The explanation is flat and repetitive, with no distinctive voice in a moment that could readily hold a light joke.
